criteria.question: Tell me about the high-intensity environment you come from — consulting, banking, VC/PE, or an early-stage startup — and how long you were in it.
criteria.source_quote: 3–4 years in a high-intensity environment. Top-tier consulting, banking, VC/PE, or an early-stage startup.
criteria.looks_like: 3-4 years in a demanding role (top-tier consulting, banking, VC/PE, or early-stage startup) where the candidate was the person things got thrown at.

criteria.question: Show me a workflow you've automated or something you've built with a coding agent — how are you already using AI agents in your real work?
criteria.source_quote: Genuinely AI-native. This is a hard requirement, not a buzzword.
criteria.looks_like: Concrete examples of using AI agents to do real work, automating a workflow, or building something with a coding agent, with ability to demonstrate it live.
criteria.hard_quote: This is a hard requirement, not a buzzword.

criteria.question: How do you handle going from a high-level strategic task to a mundane operational one, like chasing a receipt, in the same day?
criteria.source_quote: You take a strategic framing session and a receipt-chasing task in the same afternoon with the same energy.
criteria.looks_like: Examples of moving between strategic framing work and unglamorous operational tasks without losing energy or dropping either.

criteria.question: Describe a time you noticed a gap with no clear owner and stepped in without being asked.
criteria.source_quote: Extreme ownership. You see gaps, you fill them, and you don't wait to be told.
criteria.looks_like: A specific instance of identifying an unowned problem and taking it on proactively, not waiting for instructions.

criteria.question: Walk me through a time you built a financial model, structured a market analysis, and wrote up a narrative for it.
criteria.source_quote: You can build a financial model, structure a market analysis, and write a compelling narrative with equal comfort.
criteria.looks_like: Concrete examples spanning financial modeling, market/strategic analysis, and clear narrative writing, done by the same person.

criteria.question: Share a piece of writing — an investor update, a candidate email, a partnership brief — that went out without needing edits.
criteria.looks_like: Writing samples (investor updates, candidate emails, partnership briefs) that are clear, direct, and required no further editing.

criteria.question: How do you engage with engineers or direct AI agents on technical work, even though you don't write code yourself?
criteria.source_quote: You don't need to write code, but you understand how software gets built and can engage credibly with engineers - and direct AI agents that build for you.
criteria.looks_like: Evidence of understanding how software is built well enough to hold credible technical conversations with engineers and to direct AI agents to build things.

criteria.question: Can you confirm you're fluent in English, since that's the working language here?
criteria.source_quote: Fluent English. It's our working language.

criteria.question: Do you have experience in fintech, B2B SaaS, or the office-of-the-CFO space?
criteria.source_quote: Experience in fintech, B2B SaaS, or the office-of-the-CFO space
criteria.looks_like: Prior work experience within fintech, B2B SaaS, or an office-of-the-CFO function.

criteria.question: Have you worked at a startup before — as a founder, early employee, or operator?
criteria.source_quote: Prior startup experience (founding, early employee, or operator role)
criteria.looks_like: A background as a founder, early employee, or operator at a startup.

criteria.question: Have you been involved in or close to a fundraising process before?
criteria.source_quote: Exposure to fundraising processes. You've seen how rounds come together
criteria.looks_like: Direct or close exposure to how funding rounds are put together.

criteria.question: Do you speak Spanish or German?
criteria.looks_like: Conversational or working proficiency in Spanish or German.

criteria.question: How would you approach being the first person on a brand-new strategic question, like a build-vs-partner decision, before any resources are committed?
criteria.source_quote: Frame strategy before it becomes a project.
criteria.looks_like: Structuring an open-ended strategic question, running a first-pass analysis, and giving founders a direction to react to.

criteria.question: How would you manage financial operations across three entities, four banking providers, payroll, invoicing, and month-end close?
criteria.source_quote: Three entities (US, Germany, Spain), external accountants in each, banking across four providers, payroll, invoicing, spend and receipt tracking, month-end coordination.
criteria.looks_like: Ownership of multi-entity financial operations — banking, payroll, invoicing, receipts, month-end — with an eye toward automating them.

criteria.question: How would you run recruiting operations, from sourcing through structured trial days to closing a candidate?
criteria.source_quote: Source, screen, and coordinate candidates across business roles. Prepare and run our structured trial days, and help close top talent.
criteria.looks_like: End-to-end recruiting ownership: sourcing, screening, coordinating, running trial days, and helping close offers.

criteria.question: Describe how you'd extend an internal fleet of AI agents built with tools like Claude Code or Codex.
criteria.source_quote: Build with AI agents, not just spreadsheets.
criteria.looks_like: Building or extending internal AI agents so repeated manual tasks get automated rather than redone a third time.

criteria.question: How would you support the GTM engine — account research, outbound infrastructure, CRM hygiene, and event operations?
criteria.source_quote: Target account research, outbound infrastructure, CRM hygiene, event operations... from CFO dinners and conference sponsorships to hackathons we co-organize with top-tier partners.
criteria.looks_like: Hands-on GTM support spanning research, outbound systems, CRM upkeep, and running events with top-tier partners.

criteria.question: How would you act as founder leverage — handling the all-hands deck, investor updates, briefing materials, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks?
criteria.source_quote: The weekly all-hands deck, investor updates, briefing materials, speaker submissions, meeting follow-ups.
criteria.looks_like: Owning the unglamorous, high-leverage work that keeps founder time focused — decks, updates, briefings, follow-ups, and taking ownership of anything ownerless.

criteria.question: As the company grows, how would you take ownership of new, unfamiliar topics landing on your desk?
criteria.looks_like: Willingness and ability to own new topics as they arise with company growth.
